answer.rationale: Rollback is the historically clean checkout fix (memory_b1) but is forbidden because the in-flight release is a must-keep security patch. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails fast and would risk dropping settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective. The live symptom is write-path p99 at 5x during the daily settlement peak with heavy writes, which is most consistent with saturation; memory_b3 is the closest analog (headroom kept queue depth flat through a surge). Failover (memory_b2) could still be the better move if this is regional degradation rather than load, or if mid-peak provisioning is too slow—hence verifying b3 and b2. Read-replica routing is a weaker fit because the stated pressure is writes, not report/dashboard reads. Cause remains uncertain: the irrevertible release may be a regression that capacity will only partly absorb.
